sourceArticle.title: (PDF) Hot Flash Prediction for the Delivery of Just‐In‐Time Interventions
sourceArticle.author: Nader Naghavi

athenaOutput.directive: Establish a fully sovereign, edge-native biometric prediction engine and Just-In-Time Adaptive Intervention (JITAI) delivery system that anticipates hot flashes using localized wearable telemetry, guaranteeing absolute biometric data sovereignty.
athenaOutput.rationale: Physiological indicators of autonomic nervous system events (such as hot flashes) constitute highly sensitive biometric data. Under Article XXIV, this data must never be exported to the cloud. By architecting a zero-cloud, edge-processed prediction model, we ensure ultra-low-latency interventions (crucial for JITAI efficacy), constant availability regardless of network state, and strict adherence to constitutional privacy mandates.

options.title: Edge-Native Wearable Mesh (Zero-Transmission)
options.description: Deploy a lightweight, quantized prediction model directly onto the wearable hardware or a tethered local smartphone. All biometric data (heart rate variability, skin conductance, skin temperature) is ingested, analyzed, and purged locally. The JITAI is triggered directly by the edge device.
options.tradeoffs: Maximizes privacy and minimizes latency. However, it is constrained by the compute power and battery life of the edge device, requiring highly optimized, quantized ML models.

options.title: Sovereign Home Hub Processing
options.description: Wearables transmit raw biometric streams via local network (Bluetooth/Wi-Fi) to a sovereign, self-hosted Creative Liberation Engine node (e.g., NAS). The hub runs a heavier, high-fidelity prediction model and sends the intervention trigger back to the wearable.
options.tradeoffs: Allows for vastly superior predictive modeling using larger parameter models without cloud export. However, interventions may fail or degrade if the user leaves the local network environment unless a secure sovereign VPN is established.

options.title: Local Environmental & Biometric Fusion
options.description: Combine the edge-native wearable data with local IoT environmental sensors (room temperature, humidity). When a hot flash is predicted, the JITAI not only alerts the user but automatically triggers sovereign smart home interventions (e.g., lowering AC, activating fans).
options.tradeoffs: Provides a highly holistic and effective intervention. However, it significantly increases architectural complexity and requires extensive, non-standardized local IoT integrations via SIGNAL.

options.title: Federated Learning Network (Anonymized Sync)
options.description: Devices process biometric data locally to trigger JITAI, but periodically compute gradient updates based on prediction accuracy. Only these encrypted, mathematical gradients (no raw biometrics) are synced to a central sovereign node to continuously train a global model.
options.tradeoffs: Enables continuous model improvement across a fleet of users while preserving raw data privacy. However, federated learning infrastructure is highly complex to build and maintain, risking violation of Article IX if not shipped fully complete.

options.title: Haptic-Only Stealth Intervention System
options.description: Focus entirely on the delivery mechanism of the JITAI. Instead of screen-based cognitive alerts, the system uses predictive biometrics to trigger preemptive, localized cooling or specific calming haptic rhythms on the wearable before the user consciously perceives the hot flash.
options.tradeoffs: Offers a seamless, zero-friction user experience that minimizes anxiety. However, it relies heavily on specialized hardware capabilities that may not be present in off-the-shelf wearables.

options.title: Cloud-Backed API Prediction Engine
options.description: Stream biometric data to a managed third-party cloud service (e.g., AWS Health or OpenAI API) for high-accuracy prediction and JITAI generation, returning the result to the local device.
options.tradeoffs: Easiest to implement and access to massive compute. However, it fundamentally violates Article XXIV (Biometric Data Sovereignty) and Article I (Sovereignty).
